Improvement: Repair the Passport and report on phones
Observation: At 390px, the Passport title wraps almost one letter per line. The report cover also squeezes its title into a very narrow column; its academy name and date run together. This obstructs the main content.
Recommended change: Use a single-column mobile header and cover; move metadata and actions below the title. Check long names at 320, 390, 768 and 1440px and at 200% zoom.

Observation: Team & access presents 5 total and 5 active as 50% each. A group shows 7 athletes, capacity 8 and 1 open spot as 44%, 50%, 6%. These are overlapping values, not parts of a whole. Report bars retain a visible red segment for zero priorities.
Recommended change: Use plain counts for different units. Show group occupancy as 7 of 8 (87.5%). Restrict stacked percentages to mutually exclusive categories in the same population; render zero as zero. Audit the shared pulse component everywhere.

Improvement: Make event and match timing truthful
Observation: The deployed event is dated 26 September 2026, but on 11 October an upcoming match still reads “Starting now.” A paused match and a live fun event remain visible without an indication of how old their state is.
Recommended change: Derive labels from the full scheduled date, event lifecycle and last update. Distinguish upcoming, delayed, live, paused, completed and archived; show a last-updated time and event date.

Improvement: Restore report PDF generation in the reviewed environment
Observation: Preview & download PDF fails. Retrying returned HTTP 503: the local service lacks the PDF rendering native stack or a configured headless browser. This is an environment failure; production behavior was not established.
Recommended change: Package and health-check the renderer, then verify a real report preview/download. Offer an understandable retry or HTML preview while unavailable. Keep the report content accessible.

Improvement: Make entry and product boundaries obvious
Observation: The reviewed public website has product explanations and contact links but no obvious existing-user login. ChampionSpace competition records and TournamentSpace event operations are distinct, with separate registries/accounts.
Recommended change: Add an Open app entry with Academy & athlete development and Run / follow a tournament choices. Add a consistent switcher in both spaces and explain what carries over. Do not imply account or player synchronization exists.

Observation: Kavin’s report identifies Star academy while the persistent breadcrumb says Bengaluru Badminton Academy. Other academy views also retain a different global context. The interface does not clearly distinguish selected scope from the record’s academy.
Recommended change: Show the current organization, branch and role consistently. Label a cross-academy record explicitly and keep list/detail navigation in context. Verify with an administrator switching academies.

Observation: Coach home, hub, workspace, squad and classic views overlap. Sample views show 21 athletes awaiting decisions, 13 plan reviews and 38 actions without an immediately clear relationship.
Recommended change: Use one primary coach home with Today, Needs attention, Athletes and Plan. Define athlete counts versus task counts, date windows and filters. Retain specialized views as secondary destinations.

Improvement: Use familiar instructions and guard unfinished setup
Observation: The assessment workflow already has five stages, but uses terms such as SUBJECT, ARM STAGE and “lock this layer to arm the lab.” Opening the review route directly can show 0 athletes and 0 tests with a save action.
Recommended change: Use Select athletes, Choose tests, Review and Continue. Show step progress and saved/unsaved state. Redirect an empty review to setup, preserve valid drafts, and disable save until requirements are met.

Observation: Research shows illustrative benchmarks and no validated references, while other surfaces use “Certified battery,” “High confidence” or “100% confidence.” The athlete report does correctly disclose demonstration norms.
Recommended change: Carry the report’s disclosure to every score and benchmark. Distinguish reference validity, sample size, data completeness and algorithmic confidence. Suppress strong small-cohort rankings or qualify them beside the claim.

Observation: A sampled competition review shows 2 wins and 0 losses but says “the loss exposed defence under pace.” It undermines trust in the narrative. This was observed in seeded content, not proven in production-generated reviews.
Recommended change: Validate demo narratives against results. For generated summaries, derive outcome statements from recorded matches and show the supporting match.

Observation: Six bottom destinations compete for width. Some dense filters and report layouts are difficult to scan. Video analysis exposes missing-package details, and connection configuration is prominent in settings.
Recommended change: Keep the most frequent destinations visible and group secondary ones. Review touch targets and keyboard focus. Present useful recovery actions for video failures; put technical connection details behind an administrator section.

Observation: A new isolated database still opens with the Happiest Minds event identity and eight courts. Setup is spread across Players, Fixtures, Referee and Activity, while QR promotion takes early overview space.
Recommended change: Provide Event details → Players → Draw → Courts & schedule → Referees → Publish. Show incomplete items and one next action. Separate an editable event identity from a reusable template.

Improvement: Separate current data from reset templates
Observation: Activity says “No saved starting setup” but also presents a 206-player / 331-fixture official template even in an empty database. Reset controls occupy the top of the activity view.
Recommended change: Label template counts as template data. Move reset/restore into event administration, show an exact impact summary, and keep the activity feed focused on changes. Existing backup and confirmation mechanisms should be retained.

Observation: Players combines all-category import, category import, quick add and registration of an existing identity. Fixtures mixes format settings, generation, schedule downloads and match actions. Long explanations carry much of the guidance.
Recommended change: Lead with Import roster, Register existing player or Add new player. Keep the existing import preview. Use a schedule summary and change preview showing rest constraints, conflicts and any unscheduled final.

Observation: The live selector is a long list mixing finished and paused matches. A large draw opens with many early-round matches/byes. There is no clear player-focused search in the reviewed fixture view.
Recommended change: Add player/team search, round and status filters, follow-this-match links, and a current-round default. Promote live courts and upcoming matches above promotional QR panels.

Improvement: Show working screens in product explanations
Observation: The public website already contains controlled workflow slideshows, motion controls and illustrations. Many product sections still explain concepts without showing enough of the actual application.
Recommended change: Replace selected generic illustrations with annotated app captures. Show one action, its result and the next step. Keep each walkthrough to three or four frames and link directly to the relevant space.
